item.text: A metal spoon feels colder because metal conducts heat very well. When you touch it, heat quickly flows from your warm hand into the metal, cooling your skin. Wood is a poor conductor, so it takes heat from your hand much more slowly. Both spoons are actually at nearly the same room temperature—they only *feel* different because of how fast they transfer heat. Your skin senses the rate of heat loss, not temperature alone.
